title: Interface lemma models_def' re-expresses entailment over all universes for Birkhoff completeness
intent: `Completeness'` is Birkhoff's completeness theorem, and its proof is two lines of glue with no case analysis or induction: the hypothesis `h : Γ ⊧ E` is re-expressed through the interface lemma `models_def'` into a statement about the free magma with laws (quantified over every universe), instantiated at `FreeMagmaWithLaws β Γ` using `isModel` (that this magma satisfies `Γ`), and converted to a derivation with `isDerives`. The interface lemma `models_def'` is the abstraction boundary: it reformulates the bundled `models` relation, which quantifies only over `Type` (universe 0), as a universal statement over `Type*` (all universes), so the client stops unfolding `models` and stops reasoning about universes.

parent.statement: theorem Completeness' {α β} {Γ : Ctx α} {E : MagmaLaw β} (h : Γ ⊧ E) : Nonempty (Γ ⊢' E)

children.name: models_def'
children.statement:
theorem models_def' {α β} {Γ : Ctx α} {E : MagmaLaw β} :
    Γ ⊧ E ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Magma G], G ⊧ Γ → G ⊧ E
children.closed_by: constructor <;> intro H G _ h (the iff split); the two exacts close each direction (forward via models_toNat, FreeMagmaWithLaws.isDerives, Soundness'_u, satisfies_toNat; backward via satisfies_equiv uliftMagmaEquiv and satisfiesSet_equiv uliftMagmaEquiv)
children.note: The interface lemma itself. It reformulates `Γ ⊧ E` (the bundled `models`, quantified over `Type` at universe 0) as a universal statement over `Type*` (all universes), which is what lets `Completeness'` instantiate the model at `FreeMagmaWithLaws β Γ` (in `Type (max u v)`). Closes from the project siblings `FreeMagmaWithLaws.isDerives`, `FreeMagmaWithLaws.models_iff_u`, `Soundness'_u`, and the MagmaLaw lemmas `models_toNat`, `satisfies_toNat`, `satisfies_equiv`, `satisfiesSet_equiv`. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The interface lemma: semantic entailment Γ ⊧ E is equivalent to the universal statement that every magma G in any universe satisfying Γ also satisfies E.

children.name: FreeMagmaWithLaws.isDerives
children.statement:
theorem FreeMagmaWithLaws.isDerives {α β} {Γ : Ctx α} {E : MagmaLaw β} :
    FreeMagmaWithLaws β Γ ⊧ E → Nonempty (Γ ⊢' E)
children.closed_by: simp [satisfies, satisfiesPhi]; Quotient.exact; SetoidOfLaws.iff; evalInMagma_leaf; final `exact h'`
children.note: Converts a semantic fact about the free magma with laws into a syntactic derivation: `FreeMagmaWithLaws β Γ ⊧ E` implies `Nonempty (Γ ⊢' E)`. It instantiates the satisfaction at the embedding `LfEmbed Γ`, then unwinds the quotient with `Quotient.exact`, `SetoidOfLaws.iff` and `evalInMagma_leaf`. Closes on the project lemma `FreeMagmaWithLaws.evalInMagmaIsQuot` (84-94) and the `derive'`/quotient definitions. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If the free magma with laws satisfies the law E, then E is derivable from the laws Γ in the restricted calculus.

children.name: FreeMagmaWithLaws.isModel
children.statement: theorem FreeMagmaWithLaws.isModel {α} (β) (Γ : Ctx α) : FreeMagmaWithLaws β Γ ⊧ Γ
children.closed_by: intro E mem φ; PhiAsSubst; FreeMagmaWithLaws.evalInMagmaIsQuot; final `exact Quotient.sound ⟨derive'.SubstAx mem _⟩`
children.note: Shows the free magma with laws satisfies every law `E ∈ Γ`: under a valuation `φ` the term rewrites, via `PhiAsSubst` and `FreeMagmaWithLaws.evalInMagmaIsQuot`, to `Quotient.sound` of the axiom `derive'.SubstAx mem`. Closes on `PhiAsSubst` (118-121), which closes on `PhiAsSubst_aux` (112-116) via `Classical.axiomOfChoice` — the proof's one use of choice, flagged by the authors at line 111. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The free magma with laws is itself a model of the laws Γ.

applicability.goal_shape: A semantic entailment `Γ ⊧ E` (an unbundled `def models` that quantifies over models in `Type` only) that must be discharged by constructing a specific model in a larger universe; the target is an existence of a syntactic derivation `Nonempty (Γ ⊢' E)`.
applicability.use_when: the definition of the semantic relation is universe-restricted or otherwise not in a form the client can instantiate, and the client wants one canonical re-expression (an API lemma) so it stops unfolding the bundled definition; the target model is a construction (here the free magma with laws) proved separately to satisfy the context and to turn satisfaction into derivation.
applicability.avoid_when: the entailment can be discharged directly at a model already in `Type` (then no universe lift is needed and unfolding locally suffices); the re-expression is not yet the stable form clients consume, so it would be rewritten again downstream; or the two directions of the equivalence need materially different arguments, in which case the iff hides real work rather than removing it.

consequences: Creates three obligations, one per direct child: (1) the interface equivalence `models_def'` — an iff, so two directions, the forward one still needing the completeness core and the backward one a soundness fact; (2) `isModel`, that the constructed magma satisfies the laws; (3) `isDerives`, that satisfaction in the constructed magma yields a derivation. The proof relies on the axiom of choice: `isModel` reaches `PhiAsSubst_aux`, whose proof uses `Classical.axiomOfChoice` (the authors flag it at line 111: 'Sadly, we falter here and use choice. Somewhat confident it's not needed.'). It pins the reformulation: after `models_def'`, a client that wants entailment over `Type` only must still go through the `Type*` form. The sibling theorem `Completeness` (160-162) is the immediate specialisation to `derive`, so any change to the `models` definition must keep `models_def'` in sync.
